title: Reverse a Service Request Sequence
real_world_story: A banking system temporarily records a sequence of service requests. For a rollback or review operation, the system needs to process the most recently recorded request first.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A stack that returns the most recently inserted request first

problem_statement: Given N service request IDs, insert them into a stack and remove them one by one. Print the request IDs in the order in which they are removed from the stack.
task: Use stack operations to reverse the given sequence of service request IDs.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of service requests. The second line contains N space-separated request IDs.
output_format: Print the request IDs in reverse order separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: The last request inserted into the stack is the first request removed.
Stack operations follow Last-In-First-Out ordering, so the sequence is reversed.

expected_algorithm.name: Stack Operations
expected_algorithm.reason: A stack follows Last-In-First-Out ordering, which naturally reverses the order of service requests.

hint: Push every request ID onto the stack.
The last inserted request will be at the top.
Pop the stack one element at a time.
real_world_takeaway: Stack operations are useful when banking systems need to review or roll back the most recently recorded operations first.
